clue.text: Intellectual pap or something more worth chewing over?

definitions.text: Intellectual pap or something more worth chewing over?

parts.words: Intellectual pap or something more worth chewing over?
parts.note: the clue plays on eating language (pap, chewing over) for ideas that give the mind something to ponder

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an idea or remark worth pondering, pictured as nourishment for the mind.

clue.text: For instance, Cary Grant's background?

parts.note: background suggests a film star's upbringing, but means the studio scenery behind an actor such as Cary Grant

explanation.walkthrough: Cary Grant was a Hollywood film star; 'background' pretends to be his life story.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio set is literally the backdrop against which a movie actor performs.

clue.text: Theatrical action in which a part is life-enhancing

definitions.text: Theatrical action in which a part is life-enhancing

parts.words: Theatrical action in which a part is life-enhancing
parts.note: theatrical and part suggest a stage play, but the theatre is an operating theatre and the part a body organ given to a patient

explanation.definitionFit: Surgery in an operating theatre replacing a failing body part to save or improve a life.

clue.text: Insect on the outside of a pan

indicators.note: the insect word sits on the outside of the letter A, enclosing it

parts.note: a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug crawling on the outer side of a cooking pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' is not cookware but the verb meaning to criticise savagely.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a play is to criticise it harshly, a figurative sense of flaying.

clue.text: It's right to elicit contract

parts.note: educe means to draw out or elicit

explanation.surface: A statement that drawing out a contract is the proper thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, contract means to shrink or make smaller, a synonym.

clue.text: Time to get into work in Hampshire — but this attire's not for the office!

indicators.note: the work piece with its time letter goes in the county abbreviation

parts.note: Hants is the usual abbreviation of Hampshire, an English county

indicators.note: the time letter gets into the work word, sitting inside it

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone works in Hampshire but wears an outfit unsuitable for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England, abbreviated HANTS; T inside OP gives OTP, which then goes inside HANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Very short shorts are a kind of clothing, a garment hardly suited to office work.

clue.text: Like very many without identification

definitions.meaning: so numerous as to be beyond counting
lacking an identifying figure or label

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: too many to count, and not given an identifying figure.

clue.text: Man expecting to succeed at the highest level

definitions.text: Man expecting to succeed at the highest level

parts.words: Man expecting to succeed at the highest level
parts.note: sounds like an ambitious careerist, but succeed means take over from, and the highest level is the monarchy

explanation.definitionFit: The person next in line to become monarch expects to succeed the current sovereign.

clue.text: Without a stitch on, a Parisian boy will catch cold

indicators.note: the French article and boy together catch the cold letter between them

parts.note: un is French for a
a lad is a boy
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A naked French boy is sure to catch a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed means wearing no garment at all, without a single stitch.

clue.text: Pull girl round, one not keeping up

indicators.note: turning the two words round reads their letters backwards

parts.note: to drag is to pull
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: Someone drags a girl around, but one person lags behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the whole of DRAGGAL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler who falls behind the others is a laggard.

clue.text: Stress of numbers at home possessing nothing

parts.note: tens are numbers

indicators.note: the home word possesses, holding inside it, the nothing letter

parts.note: in means at home
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The strain of having a houseful of people with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress and strain are synonyms for mental or physical tightness.

clue.text: Conclusion of news, last bit broadcast

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the end is the last bit

explanation.surface: The closing moments of a news bulletin going out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the news picture but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To send a signal is to broadcast or transmit it.

clue.text: Waste material recycled in camps later

indicators.note: recycled means the letters are reprocessed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Rubbish reprocessed later in camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal for recycling is a kind of waste material.

clue.text: Legal order gets one in residence troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A court ruling brings strife to a household.
explanation.walkthrough: In English law a decree nisi is the provisional divorce order.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a provisional court order in divorce proceedings, made absolute later.

clue.text: Politicians issuing lies, apart from the leader

indicators.note: the word is taken without its first letter, its leader

parts.note: stories are lies, as in telling stories

explanation.surface: Politicians spreading falsehoods, except for the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issuing' is a link word. Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tories are politicians of the British Conservative Party.

clue.text: Watching international cricket, journalist's sworn

parts.note: at a match means watching it
a Test is an international cricket match
ed, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: A journalist at a Test match swears to what he saw.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a long international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Attested and sworn both mean formally declared true.

clue.text: Cake served in summer in guest-house

indicators.note: the answer is served inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A dessert offered in a guest house during the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A meringue is a light baked confection, loosely a small cake.

clue.text: Not a major group in the music world

definitions.text: Not a major group in the music world

parts.words: Not a major group in the music world
parts.note: sounds like a small band, but means a set of notes in music that is the opposite of major

explanation.definitionFit: In music a key is a tonal group of notes; this one is the non-major kind.

clue.text: Scotland's great mess — English left upset

parts.note: muck is mess

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the two letters upside down, reading them upwards

explanation.surface: A great mess in Scotland as the English leave in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots dialect word for large or much, used north of the border.

clue.text: Her Majesty's seen wandering around, cool as a cucumber

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit around the royal abbreviation
wandering means the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen strolls about, calm and unflustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges SEEN to SENE, which goes 'around' ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being calm and unruffled, cool as a cucumber, is a synonym.

clue.text: Squeeze out from train

definitions.meaning: to press juice out of something
a fast railway service stopping at few stations

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to press out, and a fast non-stopping railway service.

clue.text: Bit that's creased in party dress

parts.note: a do is a party
gear is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: A crumpled section of a party frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A turned-down page corner is a creased bit of a book.

clue.text: I'd cope with tyro needing textual amendment

definitions.text: I'd cope with tyro needing textual amendment

indicators.note: the letters need amending, i.e. reworking into a new order

explanation.surface: A novice's draft needs sorting out by an experienced hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A publishing professional who corrects and amends a beginner's text.

clue.text: Cold joint is something to eat

parts.note: the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A cold joint of meat to snack on.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried potato piece is an example of food.

clue.text: Star participating in 'love game'

indicators.note: the answer takes part within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A celebrity playing in a tennis game where the score is love.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Letting a bit of the countryside celebrate

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a piece of countryside
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Renting out a patch of rural land for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasing property is letting it out for rent.

clue.text: Eeyore's upset — not a pretty sight

indicators.note: an upset donkey has its letters knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: The gloomy donkey is distressed and looks dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh; the 's gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly thing is something unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Workers who cross the line and hit vandals?

parts.note: strike means hit
vandals are breakers of things

explanation.surface: Workers crossing a picket line, then assaulting wreckers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabs who work during a strike cross the picket line.
